Q1.baseline: walkable weighted graph + explicit local geometry/visibility/change descriptors + k-shortest/beam/simple feasible route pool + raw two-objective registry (interest, repeated distance) + transparent operating-point selection
Q1.author_route: claimed improved genetic algorithm with guided random-walk initialization, route crossover/mutation, elite retention and Pareto comparison; printed appendix instead returns a Dijkstra shortest path
alternatives: epsilon-constraint or multiobjective label-setting on reduced graph
orienteering/MILP/CP-SAT for a smaller candidate graph
NSGA-II/GA only if genuine nondominated search is implemented and exact methods are infeasible
not_recommended: treating a scalar weighted-fitness GA as a Pareto method without nondominated archive
accepting convergence plots as global optimality proof
using printed Dijkstra code as implementation evidence for IGA
Q1.why_select: the reusable value is the interpretable graph/scene-change representation; optimizer complexity should follow graph size and the need for a tradeoff set, not the paper label
Q1.switch_condition: use exact/bounded route search when reduced graph is tractable; promote evolutionary Pareto search only when many feasible routes remain and the implementation preserves feasibility/objective vectors

Q2.baseline: deterministic geometry/spatial/open-close descriptors + declared dimensionless ranges + independently sourced AHP pairwise judgments and/or entropy/CRITIC weights + fixed calibration scale + sensitivity + held-out expert/measurement validation
Q2.author_route: element distribution + open-close dynamics + AHP-entropy combination + final 0-100 ranking; printed code includes random surrogate features, AHP-CRITIC wording/fixed weights and hard-coded final scores
alternatives: CRITIC or entropy weighting alone with full provenance
ordinal/pairwise preference model when independent human labels are sufficient
not_recommended: random surrogate feature generation inside a real-data result path
hard-coded ranking dictionaries overriding computed model output
using the anchor/ranking itself as proof of validity
Q2.why_select: with n≈10, transparent deterministic scoring is safer than a high-capacity predictor; the first priority is provenance and independent calibration/validation
Q2.switch_condition: move to supervised preference/ranking only with more independent gardens and labels; use latent reduction when multicollinearity makes weights unstable

Q3.baseline: compact garden-level geometric/path descriptors + optional pretrained image/text embeddings when actual modalities exist + simple standardized similarity; garden-level holdout before generating pairs; external expert pair labels or downstream retrieval/classification target
Q3.author_route: geometry/image/text extractors -> MKL -> contrastive deep embedding -> feature + persistent-homology topology + HMM behavior similarity; perspective extension adds ray scoring + NeRF/STGCN/multitask regularization
alternatives: PCA/factor + cosine/Gower similarity on compact features
regularized metric learning with grouped garden holdout
pretrained CLIP/text/image embedding fusion without training a new deep network when n is tiny
not_recommended: training a new deep multimodal metric model on ~10 independent gardens without entity-level validation
pair-level random CV where the same garden appears on both sides
calling an untrained embedding or shared proxy distances topology/HMM evidence
Q3.why_select: the paper’s modality decomposition is conceptually useful, but its sample scale and printed-code incompleteness make a compact pretrained/transparent baseline substantially safer
Q3.switch_condition: promote learned multimodal metric/NeRF/STGCN only when enough independent gardens, real modalities, garden-level holdout and method-defining executable code exist
